title: 1958 AHSME Problem 50
statement: In this diagram a scheme is indicated for associating all the points of segment \(AB\) with those of segment \(A'B',\) and reciprocally. To describe this association scheme analytically, let \(x\) be the distance from a point \(P\) on \(AB\) to \(D\) and let \(y\) be the distance from the associated point \(P'\) of \(A'B'\) to \(D'.\) Then for any pair of associated points, if \(x=a,\) \(x+y\) equals:

solutions.text:
The two numbered segments are parallel, so projection through the fixed intersection point gives a linear relation between \(x\) and \(y.\) The endpoint associations shown are \((x,y)=(3,5)\) and \((x,y)=(4,1).\) The slope is \(\frac{1-5}{4-3}=-4,\) so \(y=-4x+17.\) If \(x=a,\) then \[ \begin{aligned} x+y &=a+(-4a+17)\\ &=17-3a. \end{aligned} \]

Therefore, the correct answer is C.
hints: The perspective lines in the diagram associate \(x=3\) with \(y=5\) and \(x=4\) with \(y=1\)
Because the two numbered segments are parallel, the induced relation between \(x\) and \(y\) is linear
